    Create an invasion occurrence table

    Source: R/classes-vctrs.R
    inv_occurrence.Rd

    inv_occurrence() turns a data frame of species records into an <inv_occurrence> tibble. The class remembers which columns hold the coordinates, time and species, and whether coordinates are geographic. Spread, distance, plotting and resampling functions read these columns automatically. The class survives dplyr verbs such as filter(), mutate() and arrange(); dropping a coordinate column returns a plain tibble.

    Usage

    inv_occurrence(
  .data,
  lon = NULL,
  lat = NULL,
  time = NULL,
  species = NULL,
  crs = 4326
)

is_inv_occurrence(x)

    Arguments

    .data

    A data frame, tibble or sf POINT layer. For sf input the coordinates are extracted (and transformed to WGS84 when the layer has a geographic or missing CRS) into lon and lat columns and the geometry is dropped.

    lon, lat

    <tidy-select> Columns holding longitude and latitude in decimal degrees, or x and y for projected coordinates. Ignored for sf input.

    time

    <tidy-select> Optional column with the record date or year (numeric, Date or POSIXct).

    species

    <tidy-select> Optional column with taxon names.

    crs

    Coordinate reference system of lon and lat, as an EPSG code or string. Geographic coordinates (4326, "EPSG:4326", "OGC:CRS84") use great-circle distances; anything else is treated as projected with coordinates in metres.

    x

    An object to test.

    Value

    An <inv_occurrence> tibble with the same rows and columns as .data. is_inv_occurrence() returns a single logical.

    Examples

    occ <- inv_occurrence(cane_toad, lon = lon, lat = lat, time = year,
  species = species)
occ
